---
title: "Roadmap"
---

What is planned, in the order it is planned, and the questions still open.
Changes to this page are proposals; open an issue to argue with one.

## Using it in a workflow

Researchers call it from R. Projects also need it in the flow of work:

1. **Review and exceptions.** `pii_review()` writes the findings as a
   file with a decision column for a person to fill in. A committed `.piinata.yml` holds what has been reviewed:
   fields and files that may stay, detectors turned off, thresholds, and extra
   terms. `pii_check()` reads it. An exception names a field and a reason, not
   a blanket switch.
2. **Custom patterns.** Users declare their own: a name, a regular expression
   or a function, an optional validator and a confidence. Study ids, staff
   codes and local identifiers go here.
3. **Git.** A pre-commit hook (`language: r` in `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml`) and a
   GitHub Action that scan the files a commit touches and fail on unreviewed
   findings. A Python port is on the table if no Python package does the same
   job, since most hooks run in Python environments.
4. **Redaction.** The levels are: report; drop a field; replace values
   with a placeholder of the same type; replace with a stable pseudonym, so
   joins and counts still work; and a custom function. The model is Presidio's
   split between an analyzer that returns typed spans with scores and an
   anonymizer that applies an operator per type (replace, mask, hash, redact,
   encrypt, custom). `pii_scan()` is the analyzer; `pii_redact()` is the
   anonymizer, and `pii_redact_files()` writes a clean copy beside the
   original. Still to do: JSON, and a custom function as a method.
5. **Originals out of git.** Done: `pii_ignore_originals()` adds each
   original to `.gitignore` so the clean copy can be committed. It is opt-in
   and reports what it did; it does not rewrite history, so an original
   already committed stays in the repository's past.
6. **URLs and browsing data.** A URL can carry personal data in its user,
   path and query string. A URL detector would parse with a maintained parser
   and report or strip those parts while keeping the host.

Items 1 to 3 come before redaction: a scanner people cannot quiet is one they
remove.

## Open questions

1. **Phone numbers.** Decided and built: no maintained, Java-free
   libphonenumber existed on CRAN (`dialvalidator` was archived on 2026-03-30
   and `dialr` needs Java), so the sister package
   [dialtone](https://github.com/gojiplus/dialtone) validates numbers on
   Google's libphonenumber metadata (Apache-2.0). piinata uses it when
   installed: numbers with a country code are always checked, others against
   the project's `regions`; a rejected number stops counting, and a column of
   valid numbers moves up a grade.
2. **National ids.** Decided and built: the sister package
   [idcheck](https://github.com/gojiplus/idcheck) validates identity numbers in
   C++ (Aadhaar by Verhoeff checksum, GSTIN by checksum, PAN, voter id,
   passport and Indian mobile numbers by format). piinata uses it when
   installed; a checksum match is high confidence. CRAN does have two Verhoeff
   packages, `verhoeff` and `CheckDigit`, but both are GPL and neither is
   built for scanning a column.
3. **Person names in values.** Without a model, the core can only say "short,
   capitalized, mostly distinct strings", confidence low, and cannot tell a
   column of names from a column of village names. Decided, after a review of
   GLiNER, Presidio, spaCy, Flair, Stanza, IndicNER and the R routes:
   `use_gliner()` through `reticulate::py_require()` with the Apache-2.0
   `urchade/gliner_multi_pii-v1` model, run only on columns the rules leave
   uncertain and voting on the share of rows, because it manages 2 to 40
   cells a second on a CPU. Independent tests put such models at 0.4 to 0.6
   F1 on unfamiliar text and none covers short cells, so it is trusted only
   as far as the benchmark's decoys show. Not adopted: `nametagger` (2014
   English model, non-commercial license) and Presidio as a backend.
4. **The name.** `piinata` is free on CRAN and GitHub.
